statements.status_notes: c-ares releases after 1.32.3 and before 1.34.7 can invoke a query's completion callback while the query is still linked in the channel's lookup structures, in the timeout, response and dispatch paths; if the callback frees the query (or, for ares_getaddrinfo(), its host query), c-ares then uses or frees it again, a use-after-free / double-free a remote DNS server can trigger, for example over TCP. Upstream fixed it in c-ares 1.34.7 (https://github.com/c-ares/c-ares/security/advisories/GHSA-6wfj-rwm7-3542, fix https://github.com/c-ares/c-ares/commit/1fa3b86a0b8d18fe7b60f3228a01d770feb026bc, backported to the 1.34 branch as https://github.com/c-ares/c-ares/commit/d823199b688052dcdc1646f2ab4cb8c16b1c644a, release notes https://github.com/c-ares/c-ares/releases/tag/v1.34.7). The DHI Alpine 3.23 c-ares package is built from the Alpine aports c-ares recipe and the upstream release tarball, with no added patches; Alpine records the fix at 1.34.8-r0 (aports main/c-ares APKBUILD secfixes). Checked libcares.so in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (1.34.6-r0, 1.34.8-r0, 1.34.9-r0): its embedded version string matches the package version, so 1.34.6-r0 carries the vulnerable c-ares 1.34.6 and 1.34.8-r0 and later carry releases that include the fix.

Debian fixed it in trixie in 1.34.9-1~deb13u1 (DSA-6626-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-33630). The DHI Debian 13 c-ares package is a rebuild of the Debian source, and the fixed version here is the first published DHI build based on 1.34.9-1~deb13u1. Checked libcares2 in every published build on amd64 and arm64: in that build libcares.so reports c-ares 1.34.9 and the shipped Debian changelog lists the CVE-2026-33630 fix; the only earlier published build is based on Debian 1.34.5-1+deb13u1, reports c-ares 1.34.5, does not carry the fix (its changelog does not list it), and sorts below the fixed version.
